text:
sam: Heads up — after the staged deployment at 09:42 we're seeing a spike of 5xx on /v1/generate (hosted). Error rate jumped from ~7% to ~40% on the canary slice. Logs show API gateway 502s originating from model-router. Anyone on this deploy?

ops-bot: [ALERT] svc=api-gateway status=502 rate=0.41 region=us-west-2 metric=5m avg

maria: @sam I'm on it, checking canary config. Did we flip the routing flag for model_variant?

aj: Noted. I glanced at the last charted PR — there was a change that affects ROUTE_NAMESPACE in the helm values. Locally I reproduced a 502 by simulating canary headers; logs show 'kvcache shard mismatch'.

sam: yikes. @oncall-zoe can you pause the rollout? If canary pods were created with the prod namespace env var they might be talking to prod model shards and corrupting kvcache expectations.

oncall-zoe: pausing rollout now: `kubectl rollout pause deploy/model-router -n hosted-canary`
Doing a config revert: `kubectl apply -f cm/model-router-canary-v1.yaml`

jenny: I'm creating an immediate revert PR to undo the values bump (reverting commit 3c9a2). Disabling staged-routing policy until we confirm.

maria: Quick timeline: root cause appears to be config map key `route_namespace` set to `prod` in canary release. Steps taken: 1) paused rollout 2) rolled back config 3) restarted canary pods 4) running smoke tests against /v1/generate and internal kvcache health.

aj: repro steps I used: `curl -H "X-Canary-Id: test" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate` -> gateway 502. Excerpt from logs:
```
model-router: kvcache init failed: shard mismatch (expected=42 got=7)
http: respond 502 to client
```
This matches the shard_id mismatch the router emits when it binds to the wrong namespace.

sam: CS is seeing customer errors for a small set of tenants. @jenny please coordinate outreach so support can message affected customers.

jenny: Notifying CS and Support now. Draft message: "We're aware of elevated 5xx for some hosted inference requests following a canary config change. We've paused the rollout and reverted the config. We'll follow up once the rollback is verified."

ops-bot: [RECOVERY] svc=api-gateway status=502 rate=0.04 metric=5m avg — decreased from 0.41

maria: After the rollback and pod restart, canary error rate is back to baseline (<0.5%). Latency looks stable. Keeping canary pinned to the previous config until we finish an audit.

aj: Root cause summary: templating bug in helm chart led to `route_namespace` resolving to the production namespace for canary releases when release name was omitted. Fix in PR 990 includes a templating guard + unit test for namespacing.

sam: Next actions: 1) merge PR 990 and run in staging 2) re-run canary at 5% traffic with kvcache smoke harness 3) keep the staged-routing flag off until validated 4) coordinate a short postmortem and customer follow-ups.

jenny: CS tickets created: CS-4391, CS-4392. I'll follow up with the customers impacted and post the communication thread in #customer-success.

sam: Thanks team — I'll close this thread once metrics are green for 30 minutes and CS confirms outreach.
